identity.name: Silicon dioxide
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic silicon oxide (synthetic amorphous silica used as anti-caking additive)

function.mechanism: Adsorbs moisture/oils and reduces interparticle adhesion in powders, improving flowability and limiting caking.

adi.basis: EFSA 2018 concluded no need for a numerical ADI for E551 at reported uses/use levels; EFSA 2024 particle-focused follow-up reported significant concern in some scenarios and did not identify safe levels from available data for assessed endpoints.

efsa.key_finding: E551 remains authorized, but EFSA 2024 identified concern for some population/intake scenarios involving nano-sized particles from E551.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 172.480 (direct food additive, max 2% by weight); 21 CFR 182.90 (GRAS context for migration from paper/paperboard)

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED; comments indicate ADI established at the 29th JECFA (1985) for silicon dioxide and certain silicates; entry shows last evaluated in 2017 (specification context).

concerns.summary: Chronic oral mouse work reported disrupted oral tolerance and aggravated gluten-related intestinal immunopathology after exposure to food-grade silicon dioxide.
Recent in vitro digestive-cell studies report no acute cytotoxicity but indicate sub-cytotoxic morphological and cytokine-response alterations with food-grade E551 preparations.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018 re-evaluation concluded E551 was not of safety concern at reported uses/use levels and that a numerical ADI was not needed.
JECFA maintains ADI as not specified for silicon dioxide/certain silicates.
A 2025 oral fertility/early embryonic development mouse study found no significant adverse effects up to 1000 mg/kg/day.

populations: high consumers in adolescents/adults/elderly for some categories
adi_exceedance.notes: Because EFSA/JECFA do not use a numerical ADI here, risk is framed via EFSA 2024 concern scenarios (including MOE context) rather than classic ADI exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory approval remains in place, but EFSA 2024 identified significant concern for some particle-related exposure scenarios and recent animal/mechanistic studies provide plausible gastrointestinal-immune concern signals. Evidence is mixed and does not support a high-risk designation, but uncertainty is stronger than a limited-risk profile.
key_factors: EFSA 2018 no safety concern at reported uses/use levels
EFSA 2024 concern in specific population/intake scenarios with no safe levels identified from available data for assessed endpoints
U.S. direct-use limit (21 CFR 172.480) and separate GRAS migration context (21 CFR 182.90)
Recent mixed literature: immune-tolerance concern in mice vs no reproductive toxicity at high oral dose in another mouse study
